SESSION-04 TASK-31 INVESTIGATION COMPLETE (2026-09-11 UTC) — ground truth from motionssalt/clipforge bot code + real stored data:
* SETTINGS MISMATCH (root cause of 'settings never load'): the app read/wrote INVENTED shapes. Bot truth -> watermark=branding/creator_watermark.json {creator_name} (app used 'watermark'); music default=branding/music_default.json {library_track_path} (app used 'path'); narrator=branding/tts_settings.json {voice} (this one matched); Zernio is THREE separate stores: branding/zernio_settings.json {version,enabled,auto_publish,automatic_mode,target_accounts{platform->[ids]},smart_schedule{timezone,interval_hours,preferred_time,queue_depth,start_mode,custom_start}} (app wrongly stuffed api_key+enabled in here and ignored the rest), accounts live in branding/zernio_accounts.json {accounts:[{id,platform,username,displayName,isActive,enabled,needsReconnection}]} (app never read this file), and the API key is a SEALED GitHub Actions secret named ZERNIO_API_KEY (libsodium sealed box via /actions/secrets, existence checked via actionsSecretExists) — the app wrote the plaintext key into zernio_settings.json and read it back from there, so it looked empty. Also app pushNews wrote branding/news.json{message,pushed_at_epoch}; bot uses docs/news.json {version,message,interval_hours,published_at(ISO)}.
* TORRENT 422 (root cause): GitHub Contents create-or-update requires the existing file's sha on UPDATE. App's putFile only fetched sha when an explicit 'sha' arg was passed; resumeTorrentSelection wrote jobs/<id>/stage-a-request.json (ALREADY EXISTS, created by createStageATask) WITHOUT sha -> HTTP 422 'sha wasn't supplied'. Fix: putFile always GETs the file first (404 tolerated) and includes sha when present. SECONDARY torrent bug: app read 'video_files' from torrent-selection.json but the pipeline writes 'video_candidates' [{index,path,length}] (verified in operator's real job manual-1789166700312) so the app showed 0 candidates.
* SECOND-LAUNCH CRASH: previous fixes (lazy EncryptedSharedPreferences + security-crypto 1.1.0 stable) did NOT resolve it, so root cause is elsewhere. Not provable locally (no KVM/emulator). Strategy: (a) full local assembleDebug to guarantee no compile regression; (b) harden the remaining first-vs-second-run state-restoration paths in the VM init so nothing crashes even if cached data is malformed; (c) add a lightweight startup crash-catcher that records the real stack trace to a file and surfaces it on next launch, so the operator's next run REPORTS the true cause instead of guessing.
* CUSTOM DURATION: bot TARGET_DURATIONS=[30,60,120,180,300]; app already has presets+filter chip but operator says tapping Custom gives no usable input — will surface a permanent numeric TextField + 'Custom duration (seconds)' label so input is always possible.

tasks.title: Diff recovered working code vs ClipForge's current launch/session-restore/cache code; identify divergences plausibly causing the second-open crash
tasks.notes:
DONE (session-06, 2026-09-12): diff complete. The recovered WORKING app and the current app use the IDENTICAL launch state model — EncryptedSharedPreferences CredentialStore + CacheFirstStore JSON cache under filesDir — so the fix is to restore the working app's exact launch architecture into ClipForge. Three launch-relevant divergences found, all in paths that ONLY run when saved state exists (second open):
  (1) CACHE-FIRST DROPPED: working app's VM holds CacheFirstStore instances for tasks/series/music and renders INSTANTLY from the on-disk cache via onTasksOpen()->loadFromCache(), then background refresh(). Current app imports CacheFirstStore but never instantiates it — refreshAll() in init hits the NETWORK on every open and rebuilds state from scratch, the exact anti-pattern engine/ARCHITECTURE.md forbids.
  (2) UNGUARDED refreshAll() IN INIT: original v1 (08b9d63, the version the operator says crashed) called refreshAll() from init with NO try/catch. Recovered working app never calls refreshAll() in init at all — cache load is synchronous & safe, refresh is deferred to the UI (LaunchedEffect). Current code patched v1 forward by wrapping refreshAll() in try/catch, but a Kotlin `by lazy`/stateIn initializer or a rethrown exception inside a launch still escapes; the robust fix is the working architecture (no network in init).
  (3) security-crypto VERSION: working app shipped 1.1.0-alpha06 and ran stable; session-04/05 bumped to 1.1.0 'stable' while patching forward. Returning to the recovered-working launch path (lazy-guarded store, plain-prefs fallback already present) makes the keystore race unreachable.
ROOT-CAUSE MODEL: the crash is a second-open-only state-restoration failure on the launch path (MainActivity.onCreate -> VM init -> refreshAll network + no cache render). Fix = replace the current init/refresh launch behavior with the recovered working cache-first launch architecture, adapted to ClipForge's data (TaskStatus/MusicTrack/AppSettings already have toJson/fromJson). No new dependencies.

SECOND OPEN (saved state): init reads ONLY SharedPreferences via the guarded prefs getter (absorbs failed encrypted lazy-init, plain fallback) — no network, no disk-cache parse, no throwing call; UI composes immediately; TasksScreen's LaunchedEffect then runs onTasksOpen() -> loadFromCache() wrapped in runCatching (malformed JSON -> empty list + Log.w, never throws) -> taskStore.refresh() which is fully exception-absorbing (runCatching around fetchRemote, mutex-serialized, keeps cache on failure).
